title: A second member with the same email is rejected, whatever its case
when: Registers a member, then registers another with the same email in a different case and with spaces.
then: Refused as `email_taken`. Inserting the duplicate straight into the store also fails.

title: A member with 3 active loans cannot borrow a fourth
when: Lends three tools to one member.
then: The fourth borrow is refused as `loan_limit_reached`. After one return, the fourth borrow succeeds.

title: A member with an overdue loan cannot borrow
then: At 23:59 on the due date in New York (already the next day in UTC), a second borrow succeeds. At 00:00 the next day in New York, a third borrow is refused as `member_overdue`. After the overdue loan is returned, it succeeds.

title: A tool's condition is only good or needs repair
then: A new tool is `good`; a return with condition `broken` is refused; the schema refuses `broken` written directly.

title: A tool that needs repair cannot be lent
then: Borrowing it is refused as `tool_needs_repair`.
notes: Its code is keyed by the rule it proves, as S2 keys its tests: the test is named `TL-LEND-DR05 …`, not `TL-LEND-T05 …`.

title: A tool on loan cannot be lent again until it is returned
then: A second member borrowing a tool on loan is refused as `tool_on_loan`; a direct second active loan in the store fails; after the return the second member can borrow.

title: A loan is due 14 calendar days after it starts, in the library's time zone
then: The loan starts at the clock time and its due date is the New York date 14 days later, including across a year end and when UTC is already on the next day. In another time zone (Auckland) the same instant gives a later due date. An unknown time zone is refused, and the store refuses a due date that is not a date.

title: A loan is overdue only while it is active after its due date, in the library's time zone
then: Not overdue at 23:59 on the due date in New York, though UTC is on the next day; overdue at 00:00 the next day, in summer and winter time. With the time zone set to UTC, the same instant is already overdue. Never overdue once returned.

title: A returned loan cannot be returned again
then: A second return of the same loan is refused as `already_returned`.

title: A return records the tool's condition on the loan
then: A return stores the return time, the condition and the note on the loan.

title: A registration without a name or a valid email is rejected
then: `POST /members` without a name, without an email, with a blank name, or with an invalid email gives 400 `invalid_request`.

title: Registering an email that is already registered is rejected with 409
then: A second registration with the same email in another case gives 409 `email_taken`.

title: A registration returns the new member with its ID
then: The 201 response has a whole-number ID, the trimmed name, the lower-case email and the join time.

title: A tool without a name is rejected
then: `POST /tools` without a name gives 400 `invalid_request`.

title: A new tool is in good condition and available in the catalog
then: The 201 response and `GET /tools` both show the tool as `good` and `available`.

title: A loan is returned with its due date 14 days ahead
then: `POST /loans` gives 201 with `borrowedAt` now and `dueDate` the New York date 14 days later (`2026-03-16`), with no `dueAt`. A borrow at 23:30 in New York, when UTC is on the next day, is due on the New York date plus 14.

title: An unavailable tool is refused with the reason
then: Borrowing a tool on loan gives 409 `tool_on_loan`; borrowing a damaged tool gives 409 `tool_needs_repair`.

title: A member who cannot borrow is refused with the reason
then: A member with 3 loans gets 409 `loan_limit_reached`. A member can still borrow at 23:59 on a loan's due date in New York, and gets 409 `member_overdue` from 00:00 the next day.

title: Borrowing with an unknown member or tool returns 404
then: An unknown member gives 404 `member_not_found`; an unknown tool gives 404 `tool_not_found`.

title: A return without a valid condition is rejected
then: A return with no condition or an unknown one gives 400 `invalid_condition`; an unknown loan gives 404.

title: A tool returned in good condition is available again
then: The tool shows `on_loan` while lent and `available` after a return in good condition.

title: A tool returned needing repair is taken out of lending
then: After a return needing repair, the catalog shows `needs_repair` with the return note, and borrowing it is refused.

title: A return on a day after the due date is flagged as late
then: A return at 23:59 on the due date in New York (already the next day in UTC) has `late: false`; a return at 00:00 the next day has `late: true`.

title: A librarian marks a tool as needing repair with a note
then: Without a note gives 400; with a note gives 200 and the tool shows `needs_repair` with the note; an unknown tool gives 404.

title: Marking a tool repaired returns it to lending
then: Repairing an unknown tool gives 404 `tool_not_found` and repairing a good tool 409 `tool_not_damaged`; repairing a damaged tool makes it `good` and `available`, and it can be borrowed.

title: Reporting damage on a tool on loan does not end the loan
then: After damage is reported on a lent tool, it still shows `on_loan` and the loan can be returned; after a return recorded as `good`, the tool still shows `needs_repair`.

title: A good return does not clear damage reported during the loan
then: Damage is reported on a tool on loan, then the loan is returned as `good`: the loan records `good`, but the tool stays `needs_repair` with its damage note and cannot be borrowed. Once a librarian marks it repaired, it can be borrowed.

title: A borrow with a missing or malformed ID is rejected
then: `POST /loans` with no `memberId`, a `toolId` of 0, an ID sent as a string, or an ID that is not whole gives 400 `invalid_request`.

title: The README's curl steps work against a running server
then: It passes when every answer matches and no command prints an error.
notes: Manual because it checks what a newcomer meets: the real entry point (`npm start`, which the automated tests do not run), the documented port and the README's commands as written. Run it after changing `server.ts`, the README's API section or the response shapes.

title: A damage report over 64 KB is refused with 413
when: Sends `POST /tools/{toolId}/damage` with a body of exactly 64 KB.
then:
Expects it to be read and the note saved. Sends one a byte over and expects 413 `body_too_large` with `Connection: close`, and the tool still `good`. Sends an over-limit body to `POST /members` and expects the same 413, so the limit holds on every endpoint's body, and the email is still free afterwards.

Then, over a raw socket, it sends a chunked damage report with no declared length that never ends, writing as fast as the connection allows. It expects a 413 `body_too_large` answer with `Connection: close`, and the server to close the connection within 5 seconds instead of waiting for the body to end.

title: When several borrow checks fail, the first in order is reported
then: An invalid body with an unknown member gives `invalid_request`; an unknown member and tool give `member_not_found`; a member who is both overdue and at the loan limit gets `member_overdue`; a member at the limit borrowing a damaged tool gets `loan_limit_reached`; a tool both on loan and damaged gives `tool_needs_repair`.

title: Returning an unknown or already returned loan is refused
then: A return of an unknown loan gives 404 `loan_not_found`. A second return of a loan gives 409 `already_returned`, and changes nothing: the tool keeps the condition and note of the first return.

title: Each librarian action missing its required input is refused, says what is missing, and saves nothing
when: Proves the Librarian action pattern's first rule in Lending, for each use case that follows it. Registering a member with no name or no email, adding a tool with no name, returning a loan with no condition and reporting damage with no note each give 400 with a message naming what is missing. Afterwards the email is still free, the catalog is still empty, the loan is still active and the tool keeps its condition.

title: Each successful librarian action saves its record and shows it as stored
when: Proves the Librarian action pattern's second rule in Lending, for each use case that follows it. A registered member is shown with its ID and stored name and email, and its email cannot register again. An added tool, and a tool after damage is reported, are shown exactly as the catalog then lists them, which also proves the third rule, owed here because adding a tool and reporting damage save a Tool. A returned loan is shown with its condition and note, cannot be returned again, and the tool's catalog entry reflects it.
